verdicts.claim: Clean = 21,191 (99.73% of carriable); fallbacks = 57 (56 kind-count mismatch, 1 legacy residue)
verdicts.evidence: My converter rewrites legacy syntax to brackets in reverseInlineMarkup's order and with its hasApiMarkers and literal-asterisk gating (NEW EN '*' count passed as literalAsterisks). It fills term/fn ids and em classes by order from NEW EN, and renumbers MATH/MEDIA through the English. My gate: kind multiset equal to NEW EN's, xref/docref/link target multiset equal, no legacy residue, parses. Result: 21,191 clean and 57 fallbacks, and the fallback key set is identical to theirs. Kind deltas of the fallbacks: 27 {i:-1}, 13 {i:-1,sub:-1}, plus small groups; most are glossary terms whose March source EN carried no markup (e.g. 'sp2 hybrid orbital'). My first gate found only 56. The 57th, m68843:para:fs-idp79204432, has June IS 'SCN^-^' beside {{term}}; the injector leaves that literal, and NEW EN has no sup. It appeared only after I added a gated-residue rule, so their residue rule is the better call. Gated vs ungated conversion gives 56 vs 57 fallbacks (only 3 June IS segments carry a gated form beside an API marker), which supports their 'mirrors gating' claim. Method flag: 'visible text unchanged 21,191/21,191' is nearly tautological for a markup-only rewrite. The load-bearing gate is the kind multiset, a count check that cannot see wording, terminology or untranslated text.

overall:
Carryover's measurement holds up. I wrote a fully independent parser, normalizer, converter and gate. My class labels agree with theirs on all 22,591 keys, with no off-diagonal cell. Carried (21,248), clean (21,191) and fallback (57) reproduce exactly, and the 57 fallbacks are the same keys. The normalizer control (1,562 raw → 2 normalized), the EN-drift control (18), the equation stores (121/121), the no-June prose (984,335 chars) and the char shares (70.0% / 99.7% / 70.1%) also reproduce. All 23 per-chapter rows were recounted: 409 of 460 fields are exact, and every non-exact field is explained. I found no carried source with the wrong English (0 of 21,248; the same test rejects exactly the 3 real changes), no empty June source and no truncation (<0.6× EN length in 5,384 segments of 120+ chars). Each zero has a planted positive control that fires.

Three corrections, none of which changes a headline percentage.
- (1) Identical-to-NEW-IS is 12,117 segments / ~299,196 chars, not 12,059 / 297,863. Their aggregate compared against the last occurrence of duplicated keys while everything else uses the first. 12.9% identical and 87.1% / 61.0% differing hold.
- (2) HAND REPAIR conflicts are 21, not 22 (one same-key comparison on a shifted cell). Only 9 of the 21 are wording rulings a carry would genuinely overwrite. The other 12 fix NEW-MT defects (9 'sámeind', 3 Greek letters) that the June text never had.
- (3) The re-wrap count (41) is not reproducible from the stated rule; mine gives 28.
Smaller points:
- The rule counts are per segment.
- A strict 1:1 equal-text mapping exists, so the 48 twin reuses are an alignment artifact.
- '0 positional swaps' is supported by a NEW-MT base rate of 0/163 reorders, with one June inconsistency (m68856 fissile/fissionable) that a carry would keep.

What the structural gate cannot see, which matters for the decision:
- (a) 'Differ' mostly means moderate rewording. Of the 2.02M differing EN chars, 16.7% are in segments with token similarity >=0.95, 69.6% at 0.80-0.95, 12.5% at 0.50-0.80 and 1.2% below 0.50.
- (b) A June carry brings June's terminology back. In ch20, 31 of the 37 clean-carried segments containing 'hydrocarbon' use 'kolvetni' (carbohydrate). The NEW IS uses vetniskolefni in 64 of 65 such segments and kolvetni in 0. Any carry must therefore be followed by applying the term rulings.
- (c) ch00 would carry 5 preface segments that June left in English (2,072 chars).
- (d) A 'keep new' path inherits NEW-MT defects seen while sampling: 'Tengifákeppni' (roughly 'linkage oligopoly') for linkage isomers in m68843, and a precision/accuracy vocabulary flip in m68690, where nákvæmni is used for accuracy. There are also 21 MT-invented <lágvísir>/<subscript> tags in 3 alt segments, and 165 ~x~ plus 93 ^x^ legacy-style sub/sup strings in the NEW IS.
